sections.overview: This Lesser Antillean gecko occurs on Guadeloupe and nearby islands, Dominica and Montserrat. Its range differs from that of the Greater Antillean congener Sphaerodactylus elegans.
sections.identification: The Reptile Database lists several geographically restricted named forms and notes that phyzacinus is now treated as a valid species.
sections.habitat: On Dominica, the named form fuga has been reported in relatively moist microhabitats along the western coast.
sections.diet: The field study reviewed here does not report prey or establish a species-specific diet.
sections.behavior: The cited Dominica study measures population density and water loss, rather than providing a broader behavioral account.
sections.reproduction: The Reptile Database records it as oviparous.
sections.ecology: Its named island forms have localized ranges; see Sphaerodactylus elegans for a congener native to Cuba and Hispaniola and introduced in Florida.
sections.conservation: The 2022 Guadeloupe Red List assigns this gecko Least Concern regionally and globally; that assessment predates the current separation of S. phyzacinus as a valid species.
